paragraphs: One-sentence judgement: a team assembler does not simply put parts together but prepares, positions, fastens, connects, assembles and inspects materials under a fixed takt time according to drawings and processes, and is responsible for non-conforming products and abnormalities. The role links repeatable assembly tasks, on-site judgement and record responsibility into a reviewable work chain; people who only pursue speed of movement and are unwilling to record and report are not suited.

Signals for continued exploration: you can check versions and parts against drawings and work orders, are willing to keep checking during repetitive actions and to interrupt the takt time and report when something is abnormal, can accept job rotation and state unfinished items clearly in handover, and are willing to write processes, inspections and abnormalities as reviewable records.

Conditions for pausing investment first: you have not yet completed a full-process exercise from work order through assembly and inspection to abnormality reporting, or you can only rely on others to judge defects and stop the line for you; also do not treat gaming, hands-on interest or a short training certificate as proof of general assembly qualification.

Education and training must be checked separately: BLS lists the entry-level education for this occupation as high school or equivalent and the on-the-job training as moderate-term; O*NET lists 51-2092.00 as requiring little preparation, but posts such as precision assembly, welding and aviation assembly have separate experience and training requirements. Safety and quality requirements (machine guarding, lockout/tagout, ergonomics, inspection standards) are determined by employer procedures and customer standards, and this page provides no hiring or certification standard.

In one sentence: this is a manufacturing post whose core duties are completing physical assembly according to drawings and processes, holding the process and final inspection, and recording truthfully and reporting abnormalities. Competence depends on process compliance, attention to detail, abnormality communication and safety boundaries, not personality labels.

The work of team assemblers falls into four categories: assembly execution (completing part preparation, positioning, fastening, connection and assembly according to drawings, processes and work orders); process and final inspection (checking dimensions, appearance and function against inspection standards, isolating non-conforming products and recording the reason); equipment and tooling maintenance (using and daily checking tools, fixtures and equipment by procedure, stopping and reporting for repair when an abnormality is found); and records and collaboration (filling in production and inspection records, taking part in job rotation and synchronising with the team in handover and abnormality escalation). All four categories must be carried out within the employer's process, safety and quality system and leave reviewable on-site and record evidence.

O*NET 51-2092.00 Team Assemblers (updated 2026) describes a team jointly responsible for the whole product or component, able to rotate through most or all assembly tasks, and also includes team leaders working within the team and possibly taking part in management decisions. The tasks include quality checks, checking work orders and drawings, rotation, allocating work and mentoring, and production reports, and do not mean every post carries out all tasks. The larger BLS Assemblers and Fabricators occupation group manufactures finished goods and parts, and its wages and employment are not used directly as a precise statistic for this occupation.

entries: Work orders and drawings｜O*NET lists checking work orders and drawings to ensure specifications are met; the specific version and material checking rules should be confirmed with the employer.
Team rotation｜Rotation follows the production flow; not every assembler permanently performs only one action, and the specific operation and equipment vary with the product.

Assembly and connection｜The BLS occupation group uses tools and machines to assemble; deburring, press fitting, riveting and torque control are examples of specific operations and cannot be treated as uniform tasks for everyone in this occupation.
Quality checks｜O*NET lists checks of product and part quality; the specific inspection decision, marking and isolation and release authority must be checked against the employer's quality system.

Records and collaboration｜O*NET lists production reports and communicating team output to management; the record items and correction rules must be checked against the actual system, and full traceability is not guaranteed.

Management and mentoring｜O*NET includes work allocation and training supervision tasks and also team leaders working within the team; it cannot be asserted that this occupation has no management duty at all or that everyone has one.

paragraphs: BLS occupation group background: most work in manufacturing plants, may stand or sit for long periods, mostly full time, with some evenings and weekends; a fixed takt time for every workstation cannot be inferred from this. This O*NET occupation includes quality checks, rotation, reports, some mentoring and maintenance tasks, and the specific equipment, inspection release and process change authority must be checked against the post. Machine guarding and hazardous energy control in general US industry must be checked against the applicable rules, and maintenance differs from routine production and authorised personnel differ from affected personnel, so lockout/tagout execution authority is not given to all assemblers. The OOH high school or equivalent education and moderate-term on-the-job training is an occupation group overview; the current O*NET Job Zone is 1—2, and training varies with the post.
Assembly execution and inspection

US wage distribution: the BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS) for 2025 shown by O*NET give, on the Miscellaneous Assemblers and Fabricators measure, annual wages of 33,280 US dollars at the 10th percentile, 37,380 at the 25th, a median of 44,650, 51,200 at the 75th and 64,880 at the 90th; the corresponding hourly wages are 16.00, 17.97, 21.47, 24.61 and 31.19 US dollars. The BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook gives, on the Assemblers and Fabricators measure, a May 2025 median annual wage of 45,450 US dollars and a median hourly wage of 21.85 US dollars. The two measures differ and cannot be mixed.

Receive the work order and drawings: check the version, material and quantity. → Prepare and position: complete part preparation, positioning and clamping according to the process. → Assemble and fasten: complete fastening and connection according to the sequence and torque requirements. → In-process inspection: check dimensions, appearance and function against the inspection standards. → Record and hand over: fill in records, isolate non-conforming products and synchronise unfinished items. → Review and improve: take part in abnormality reviews and feed process problems back to the process and quality posts.

Mainland China side: the National Bureau of Statistics, Average Annual Wages of Urban Unit Employees in 2025 (released 2026-05-15) shows 129,441 yuan per year for national urban non-private units and 71,590 yuan per year for urban private units; for manufacturing the figures are 113,594 yuan per year for non-private and 76,055 yuan per year for private units; production, manufacturing and related personnel in above-scale enterprises are 80,739 yuan per year. These are industry and broad job category average wages that mix a large number of posts and cannot be used to derive a median or starting pay for team assemblers.
Safety, quality and records

Employment and outlook: the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook shows about 1,799,500 Assemblers and Fabricators employed in 2025, 1% growth projected for 2025—2035 (slower than average), a net increase of about 16,700 jobs and about 177,500 openings per year on average, mostly from replacing retirees or people changing occupation. That measure is an occupation group, not the precise headcount of team assemblers.

Confirm the work order and authorisation: check the drawing version, process documents and your own post authorisation. → Check materials and tools: check whether incoming material, fixtures and equipment are serviceable. → Assemble in sequence: complete positioning, fastening and connection in the established sequence and parameters. → Self-check and marking: self-check to standard, mark the status and isolate non-conforming products. → Report and escalate: when an abnormality is found, stop by procedure, report and record. → Hand over and review: state unfinished items clearly in handover and take part in review.

O*NET shows the Miscellaneous Assemblers and Fabricators industry background: manufacturing 76%, administrative and support services 12%, and other (including wholesale trade) 12%, which is not an independent distribution for this detailed occupation. 2025 US hiring software signals: Excel/Office 2% each, Outlook/SAP 1% each, Word/PowerPoint below 1%, and no percentage provided for AutoCAD; the denominator is associated unique job postings, not tool or AI adoption rates. The BLS larger occupation group factory and working hours background does not infer the conditions of a specific employer.

Working with fellow assemblers in the group, the team leader, quality inspectors, and process and equipment maintenance staff; when a process, material or equipment abnormality occurs, report by procedure and do not change the design or parameters yourself.

Team assemblers complete physical assembly under an established process and hold the inspection; industrial production managers configure capacity, personnel and delivery; industrial engineers and manufacturing engineers design and improve processes, fixtures and manufacturing systems; mechanical engineers are responsible for product mechanical design; electrical and electronic engineering technicians are responsible for electrical testing and commissioning. On-site feedback can be raised, but design change and signing responsibility do not lie with the assembly post.
Reviewable deliverables
Completing qualified physical assembly under the established takt time and process so that quantity, status, inspection results and records are consistent with one another.
Task objects

The objects are parts and materials, drawings and work orders, fixtures and tooling, gauges and inspection standards, and production and quality records; the basis is the employer's process documents, safety procedures and quality system.

Team assemblers (US side O*NET 51-2092.00, Team Assemblers) prepare, position, fasten, connect, assemble and inspect materials and components under a fixed takt time according to drawings, processes and work orders, isolate non-conforming products to standard and record truthfully and report abnormalities. BLS describes this occupation group as manufacturing finished products and their parts. (Original text: Assemble products, following work instructions and specifications, using handtools, power tools, and measuring instruments.) The occupation in the United States is usually entered with a high school or equivalent education and moderate-term on-the-job training; O*NET lists 51-2092.00 as requiring little preparation. Mainland China statistics aggregate by manufacturing industry sector and broad job category and do not list this occupation separately, so industry figures can only serve as a broad comparison and cannot be treated as the wage for this occupation. This page does not constitute a basis for hiring, safe operation or product acceptance decisions.
Typical flow
Receive the work order and drawings → prepare and position → assemble and fasten → in-process and final inspection → record, mark and hand over.
Acceptable outputs
Qualified assembly results, complete inspection and production records, correct isolation and marking of non-conforming products, and traceable abnormality escalation records.
Responsible party

Assembly execution and self-check are borne by the assembler; inspection decisions and release are the responsibility of authorised personnel under the employer's quality system; process, design and equipment repair are the responsibility of the corresponding engineering or maintenance posts.
Education and training

BLS lists the entry-level education as high school or equivalent and the on-the-job training as moderate-term; O*NET lists 51-2092.00 as requiring little preparation. Advanced assembly, welding or precision assembly posts have separate experience, training or certification requirements set by the employer, and this page does not provide the standard content.
Not interchangeable

Education, on-the-job training, internal certification and post authorisation are different states: a short course cannot automatically create post authorisation, and a certificate cannot replace on-site ability and safety responsibility.

At least six items must be verified before starting: the occupational measure and post entity (O*NET 51-2092.00 is the US measure, and in mainland China the post must be identified as which kind of assembly in manufacturing); education and training requirements (set by the employer and industry); safety and operating procedures (machine guarding, lockout/tagout, ergonomics and hazardous materials); quality and inspection standards (customer and employer standards); record and traceability requirements; and the pay and working hours structure (piece rates, shifts and overtime rules).
Occupational measure

On the US side it is O*NET 51-2092.00 (Team Assemblers); in mainland China first identify which manufacturing industry and which operation the post belongs to, because the assembly tasks, equipment and safety requirements differ greatly between industries.
Education and training

BLS lists high school or equivalent entry and moderate-term on-the-job training; O*NET lists it as requiring little preparation. Precision assembly, welding or aviation assembly posts have longer training requirements.
Safety and procedures

Machine guarding, lockout/tagout, ergonomics, hazardous materials and personal protection are determined by employer and regulatory requirements; when equipment or environment abnormalities are found, stop by procedure and report, and safety steps must not be skipped in order to rush the job.
Quality and inspection

The inspection standards, sampling method and release authority are determined by the employer's quality system and customer requirements; assemblers self-check to standard and isolate non-conforming products, and the decision and release are the responsibility of authorised personnel.
Records and traceability

Production quantity, inspection results, non-conforming product handling and abnormality escalation must be recorded truthfully; records are the basis for quality traceability and accountability and must not be filled in by another person or changed afterwards without a trace.
Pay and working hours

Posts with the same title may use an hourly rate, a piece rate or a shift allowance; when comparing, include guaranteed hours, overtime and shift rules, the piece rate and safety training time in the written conditions, not only the nominal hourly rate.

Team assemblers and manufacturing engineers
Responsible for the mechanical design and calculations of the product; assemblers assemble to the drawing and do not modify the design or tolerances.

If you would rather do mechanical design and calculations and be responsible for the design, compare mechanical engineers first; if you would rather build the product to the drawing, team assembler suits you.
Designing the product's mechanical structure, tolerances and materials, with outputs mainly drawings, technical specifications and design validation.
Team assemblers and mechanical engineers

Responsible for electrical testing, commissioning and fault diagnosis and for the test conclusions; assemblers complete electrical connections and visual checks to process and do not bear test release.

If you would rather do electrical testing and fault diagnosis, compare electrical and electronic engineering technicians first; if you would rather complete assembly and self-check to process, team assembler suits you.
Building and commissioning electrical systems, carrying out tests and recording data, with outputs mainly test reports and fault diagnosis conclusions.
Team assemblers and electrical and electronic engineering technicians
Centred on cutting and machining parts, requiring machine tool and machining process skills; assemblers are centred on assembly and connection and usually do not carry out part machining.
If you would rather operate machine tools to machine parts, compare machinists first; if you would rather assemble parts into a complete product and hold the inspection, team assembler suits you.
Operating machine tools to machine metal parts to drawing, with outputs mainly qualified parts and machining parameter records.
Team assemblers and machinists

Conclusion: the basis for choosing a direction is the main output, the required skills and the authorisation chain, not how similar the occupational titles sound; once the direction is decided, verify the education, training, qualification and safety requirements of the target direction item by item.

entries.answer: Team assemblers complete part preparation, positioning, fastening, connection and assembly to drawings, processes and work orders, self-check, mark and isolate non-conforming products to the inspection standards, and also fill in production and inspection records, take part in job rotation and report abnormalities; it is not mere repetitive action but keeping the assembly result, inspection status and records consistent with one another.
entries.question: What does a team assembler do every day?

entries.answer: Industrial production managers organise capacity, personnel and delivery; industrial engineers and manufacturing engineers design and improve processes, fixtures and manufacturing systems; mechanical engineers are responsible for product mechanical design; electrical and electronic engineering technicians are responsible for electrical testing and commissioning; machinists are responsible for cutting and machining parts. Team assemblers complete physical assembly under an established process and hold the inspection, and on-site feedback can be raised, but design change and signing responsibility do not lie with the assembly post.
entries.question: What is the difference between team assemblers and adjacent occupations?

entries.answer: Look at observable behaviour: whether you execute steadily to drawings and sequence, keep up checks during repetitive actions, stop and report when an abnormality is found, and record truthfully and hand over. O*NET lists the interest code for this occupation as R (Realistic), but a matching interest only indicates a close direction and cannot replace drawing reading, measurement and inspection ability.
entries.question: How do I judge whether I am suited to being a team assembler?

entries.answer: Steps that may be assisted: organising digital work orders and process documents, recording and pre-screening imaging and measurement data, summarising production and inspection data, and scheduling and takt time prompts. But drawing-based assembly, on-site dimensional and appearance decisions, non-conforming product handling, equipment checks and line stopping reporting responsibility remain with people; the degree of task automation and the number of jobs are different questions.
entries.question: Which tasks will AI change?

entries.answer: Drawing and process version confirmation, incoming material and part checking, dimensional and appearance decisions, non-conforming product isolation and release, equipment status and safety judgement, and abnormality stop and reporting decisions. These steps are borne by assemblers and authorised posts according to the employer's process, safety and quality system, and tool output must be checked by a person and cannot be a basis for release.
entries.question: Which steps must keep human review?

entries.answer: US side: BLS lists the entry-level education as high school or equivalent with moderate-term on-the-job training; O*NET lists it as requiring little preparation; precision assembly, welding and electrical work have separate training or certificate requirements. Mainland China side: mainly on-the-job training and skill grade certificates, and special operations require a certificate according to the competent department's requirements. The specific standards are set by the employer and industry, and this page does not provide the standard content.
entries.question: What qualifications must be verified to enter team assembler work?

entries.answer: Four types of risk need to be judged in advance: wrong drawing version and sequence, non-conforming products not isolated, violations of equipment and safety rules (machine guarding, lockout/tagout), and leakage of drawings and production data together with false records. The control method is to verify by procedure, stop and report and record truthfully, and safety and inspection steps must not be skipped in order to rush the job.
entries.question: Where are the occupational risk boundaries for team assemblers?

entries.answer: BLS projects 1% growth for the Assemblers and Fabricators occupation group in 2025—2035 and about 177,500 openings per year on average, mostly from replacing retirees or people changing occupation; that measure is an occupation group. Directions one can transfer to include industrial production managers, industrial engineers, manufacturing engineers, mechanical engineers, electrical and electronic engineering technicians, industrial machinery mechanics, welding and cutting personnel and production and operations first-line supervisors, but the training, qualification and responsibility boundaries of each direction differ.
entries.question: How should the outlook and transfers for team assemblers be judged?

entries.answer: Because the wage percentile measure shown by O*NET is Miscellaneous Assemblers and Fabricators (May 2025 OEWS) while the employment and projection measure in the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook is the Assemblers and Fabricators occupation group; the two have different coverage and data periods, cannot be mixed, and cannot be extrapolated to wages in mainland China.
entries.question: Why are there two measures for team assembler wages?

entries.answer: Common misconceptions include: that hands-on interest or a short course certificate is enough to obtain post authorisation (in fact employer training and assessment are required); that assembly is only repetitive action and needs no judgement (in fact drawing reading, measurement, inspection and abnormality reporting are needed); that one can move between industries by job title (in fact the process, equipment and safety requirements differ greatly by industry); and that automation has already wholly replaced this occupation (in fact the official projection is 1% growth for 2025—2035, and task automation does not equal the disappearance of jobs).

subject.name: Team assemblers
subject.summary: Team assemblers prepare, position, fasten, connect, assemble and inspect materials and components under a fixed takt time according to drawings, processes and work orders, isolate non-conforming products to standard and record truthfully and report abnormalities. On the US side this corresponds to O*NET 51-2092.00 (Team Assemblers, Bright Outlook), usually entered with a high school or equivalent education and moderate-term on-the-job training; mainland China statistics aggregate by manufacturing industry and broad job category and do not list this occupation separately, so industry figures serve only as a comparison.
